messages:
yuki: nightly-evals: noticed a 12% drop in ja chrF and ~8 BLEU points for en->ja on the new quantized build :eyes:

eval-bot: nightly eval results uploaded: https://ci/redwood/evals/175240 - summary attached (chrF, BLEU, exact-match per-prompt)

yuki: example failing prompt set is `translate_news_ja_v2` — failures show weird spacing and duplicated punctuation in outputs

sanjeev: can you paste a couple of raw examples?

yuki: sure — baseline (fp16) vs quantized (int8) below:

---

baseline: 日本の経済成長は予想を上回りました。

quantized: 日 本 の 経 済 成 長 は 予 想 を 上回り ま し た 。

---

baseline (ar): الاقتصاد العالمي يتعافى ببطء.

quantized (ar): .بطئ ة ب يتعافى العالمي الاقتصاد

---

yuki: note the inserted spaces between CJK characters and reversed punctuation in Arabic outputs (period moved to start)

amir: that looks like tokenization normalization got applied differently during sampling/decoding. maybe whitespace-tokenizer fallback? :thinking:

greg: could be pretokenizer NFKC/NFKD change. We saw similar when we switched the sentencepiece wrapper in runtime-2.1

tae-kwon: I ran `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizers/ja.json').pre_tokenizer)"` and got different pre_tokenizer object on the quantized runtime container vs baseline image (missing `SplitCJK`).

sanjeev: if SplitCJK missing, tokenizer will emit char-level tokens with spaces inserted at decode - consistent with the CJK example

amir: for AR, punctuation/directionality: check bidi handling and the `keep_bidi_marks` flag in our postprocessor. Also look at the normalize_unicode setting (NFKC can change Arabic diacritics positions)

yuki: good call. attaching failing prompt IDs and full logs: https://ci/redwood/evals/175240/failures.json (first 30 entries are mostly ja/ar)

eval-bot: rerun job queued as `175240-repro` (cmd: ./scripts/run_eval.sh --model quant-v2 --prompts translate_news_ja_v2,translate_news_ar_v1 --save-debug)

greg: triage plan:
1) Re-run on fp16 unquantized image on same machine to confirm quantization vs image drift.
2) Dump tokenizer config from both images: `cat /opt/tokenizers/ja.json` and `sha256sum` both files.
3) Run decode-only pipeline with identical token ids to see if decoder is introducing spacing.
4) Check runtime build logs for upstream `huggingface/tokenizers` version changes.

sanjeev: ownership:
- sanjeev: run (1) and (2)
- tae-kwon: run (3) compare decode/token outputs (I can instrument the decoder to print token strings)
- amir: check bidi/normalization flags and AR postprocessor behavior
- yuki: collect failing prompt set & add to regression suite if confirmed

yuki: quick note — metrics dip also shows correlation with certain buckets (short < 30 char and long > 200 char). Might be tokenizer boundary effects

amir: if it's a tokenizer binary mismatch, it could have been introduced by packaging step in release pipeline that accidentally pulled in a newer tokenizers wheel for the quantized image

greg: I've opened a release-check PR to pin tokenizers in the quantized build: https://git.redwood/release/pins/1234

yuki: thanks — if we confirm, we'll revert or add a patch to runtime to force SplitCJK and original unicode normalizer settings

sanjeev: quick run done on fp16 baseline image: metrics match nightly baseline (no drop). So likely quant image change.

tae-kwon: I dumped token ids for the same input across images — ids are different (tokenizer behavior changed), so decoding differences are expected. I'll attach diffs after instrumented run.

yuki: ok urgent next steps: stop the rolling quantized rollout for the `quant-v2` tag, rerun CI for packaging to verify wheel versions, and add failing prompt set to blocking list for canary. @ops ?:thumbsup:

greg: paused rollout and added `translate_news_ja_v2` + `translate_news_ar_v1` to canary-blocklist.

amir: patch idea: add an explicit tokenizer sanity check in image startup that runs a short set of canonical inputs and fails if outputs differ from golden. Saves us from silent tokenizer regressions.

yuki: love that — file an RFC? I'll write a short proposal and ping infra/security about the startup check implications.

sanjeev: I'll post the diff artifacts once tae-kwon uploads them. Thanks all — nice catch by nightly evals :raised_hands:

(eval-bot): job `175240-repro` finished: mismatch confirmed, artifacts: https://ci/redwood/evals/175240/repro_artifacts.zip

yuki: leaving follow-ups in jira: RED-3456 (tokenizer regression quant-v2), RED-3457 (add startup sanity checks).

greg: ping me on next steps, I'll coordinate release/pinning.
